Axolotl 0.3.0 closes the gaps that ports of four real Java libraries found: interfaces may give their methods a
body, enums may have methods, `Float` is a primitive, a pipe may build a list with nullable elements, and a
library's own `requireNonNull` messages survive. Gradle rebuilds take about half the time.

## Downloads

The installers bring their own Java runtime, put `axl` on the `PATH` and run `axl setup`, which
copies the Axolotl libraries and the Gradle and Maven plugins into the local Maven repository:

- `axolotl-0.3.0-windows-x64-setup.exe`: Windows. Not signed, so SmartScreen asks first: *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
- `axolotl-0.3.0-macos-arm64.pkg`: macOS on Apple silicon. Not signed: see the [installation guide](https://github.com/sora-vuv/axolotl-lang/blob/v0.3.0/docs/install.md) for how to open it.
- `axolotl-0.3.0-linux-amd64.deb`: Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 or newer: `sudo apt install ./axolotl-0.3.0-linux-amd64.deb`.
- `axolotl-0.3.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`: other Linux systems. Unpack it and run `install.sh`, which needs no root.

Guides to installing and using the `axl` command line, in English and Russian:
`axolotl-0.3.0-windows-en.pdf`, `axolotl-0.3.0-macos-en.pdf`, `axolotl-0.3.0-linux-en.pdf` and the
`-ru` versions.

Without an installer:

- `axl-0.3.0.zip`: the command line compiler for Java 21. Unzip it, put `bin` on your `PATH` and run
  `axl setup` for the Gradle and Maven plugins.
- `axolotl-0.3.0.vsix`: the VS Code extension: `code --install-extension axolotl-0.3.0.vsix`.
- `axl-intellij-0.3.0.zip`: the IntelliJ IDEA plugin: *Settings | Plugins | Install Plugin from Disk*.

The Gradle and Maven plugins are not published to a public repository yet: `axl setup` installs them
into the local Maven repository, and projects find them there with `mavenLocal()`.

## What is new

Language:

- Interface methods with a body, which Java sees as default methods: shared behaviour without abstract classes.
  They read the interface's values by name; `private fn` helpers and `super.m()` from an override work too.
- Enums may have methods after their constants and implement interfaces.
- `Float` is Java's `float`, with `1.5f` literals, so Java callers reach `Float` overloads and classes can override
  `float` methods or extend `Number`. **Breaking:** write `Float?` where `java.lang.Float` was meant.
- A pipe's `map` that may give null builds a `List<T?>` wherever nothing needs non-null elements.
- `use (hold(lock)) { ... }` without a name, constructors that pass their values to other constructors, `super.m()`
  in classes with a Java superclass, typed handlers that catch undeclared checked exceptions, and `Character(code)`.
- A function that begins with `Objects.requireNonNull(p, "p is null")` keeps the library's own message instead of
  the generated parameter check.

Tools:

- Gradle keeps Error Prone and NullAway loaded between compilations: a rebuild takes half the CPU time.
- IntelliJ reads the module's classpath for its checks, as `axl check` does.
- Many compiler fixes: private types in an interface's file, types of a file in its class header, `@Override` on
  `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString`, cross-file property types, counting loops over Java values, and error columns.

Quality: the fourth library port, minimal-json, passes 446 of 457 of its own tests after small edits (457 with the
module's parameter checks off), with 30% fewer lines than the Java.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/sora-vuv/axolotl-lang/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

## Known limitations

- Classes are final and there are no abstract classes; interfaces with method bodies cover most uses.
- An Axolotl library shows Java callers lists instead of arrays and no `throws`; the language guide shows the small
  Java interface that adapts such a class where Java callers need more.
- A pipe with a nullable `map` passed straight as an argument still needs a `val` first.
- Error Prone in Maven needs `.mvn/jvm.config`, and Gradle compiles in a forked JVM.
- The compiler daemon is tested on Linux; on Windows it is used only from a console.
